# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

This is a small Next.js site with four routes, and all of them were read from code. Every applicable rule is Clear and nothing is unknown, apart from what a live server or CDN decides (see "Can't tell from code").

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing is broken, so these are optional improvements. The first is the largest unknown.

### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your hosting
- **Why it matters:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall blocks the search crawlers that `robots.txt` allows.
- **Where:** your server or CDN access logs. This isn't in the repository.
- **What the code says:** `public/robots.txt:2`: `Allow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** stays 100 either way, because bot protection isn't part of any scored rule. It only confirms the result.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is reachable and valid | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, plain text, valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-3`. Policy is allow, and no search crawler is blocked. |
| GEO-014 | Linked and sitemap routes are indexable | Clear | Not run | 3 of 3 routes. `/account` is a deliberate noindex (`app/account/page.tsx:1`) and is not in the sitemap or nav. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | Not run | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`, `app/visit/page.tsx:1` |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Clear | Not run | Server Components in `app/*/page.tsx`, with no client-only fetching |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is discoverable | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml`, and `public/robots.txt:11` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. Title and description are on 3 of 3 indexable routes. |
| GEO-016 | Routes are linked with real links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:7` uses `<a href>` for all three pages |
| GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions against AI search | Clear | Not run | No page-wide `nosnippet`. Only an element-level `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:9`, which is a deliberate choice. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read the layout and all pages. There are no images, and the links have text. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app profile declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. Informational only, and not scored. |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

- **Say how to get there:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Opening times and directions.'`. The page body is only `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` and has no directions or address. Adding them in text would match what the description promises.
- **Label the opening hours:** `app/visit/page.tsx:4`: `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` Once an address is on the page, `LocalBusiness` structured data could label the hours and location for machines.
- **Back up the variety claim:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` Only two varieties are named. A list, or a page per variety, would give readers and machines the answer to "which varieties?".
- **Apply the training-crawler policy fully:** `geo.config.json` has `"trainingCrawlers": "block"`, but `public/robots.txt:5-9` names only `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot`. If you want the block to be broader, add the other training crawlers you care about.
- **Add dates to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `<url><loc>https://www.orchard.example/</loc></url>`. If you have real update dates, a `<lastmod>` on each URL gives crawlers a freshness signal.
- **Give the home page more onward links:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Grown in Herefordshire since 1952.` The page has no links to varieties or visiting beyond the menu. Links in the text could help visitors.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Real status codes and headers:** whether `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` and the pages answer 200, and whether any `X-Robots-Tag` header is set outside the repository, needs a live check.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find this site. `geo.config.json` says `"aiSearchCrawlers": "allow"`.
- `/account` is private and meant to be noindex, so I left it out of the indexable route count.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command if you want help with any item above. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
